title: Miri Standard Check Definition (v2)
description:
Schema for the per-check definition files in standards/<target>/checks/ - the canonical, machine-readable source of truth for every check, consumed by linter implementations.

WHY v2. The shape of a check definition did not change; the MEANING of one of its fields did. At 0.5.0 `conditional: true` stopped meaning 'award full weight when the condition does not apply' and started meaning 'excluded from both the numerator and the denominator'. Every value in every file stayed byte-identical, so a linter could re-sync the corpus, validate every definition against v1, and keep computing the old arithmetic with every score silently wrong. A schema is an interpretation contract, and this one's contract changed, so it gets a version.

check-v1.json is frozen and still describes pre-0.5.0 semantics. A consumer pinned to it is not wrong, only old, and stays internally consistent. What must not happen is a corpus written for v2 being read under v1: hence the required `$schema` key below, which makes that pairing fail on both sides rather than validate quietly.

id.description: Stable check ID; never renumbered. Producer targets are PY and CLI; consumption targets are CONSUMER (a metadata consumer) and SURFACE (a metadata-query surface). Extension (health-only) checks use the matching X namespace and carry weight 0.

name.description: Short human-readable name of the check

target.description: Artifact type this alert applies to

status.description: Withdrawn checks keep their file and ID; their weight is redistributed in a minor version

added_in.description: Checklist version that introduced this check

withdrawn_in.description: Checklist version that withdrew this check; required when status is withdrawn

level.description: MUST failures make the artifact non-conforming (score capped at 74)

category.description: Checklist category the check belongs to

scoring.description: How this check participates in the conformance score. `scored` (the default) contributes its weight to the numerator when it passes and to the denominator when it applies. `gate` contributes to NEITHER: it carries weight 0, and failing it makes the artifact non-conforming - which is already what a failing MUST does through the 74 cap. Gating exists for checks that are preconditions rather than measurements: MIRI-PY-001 to 003 are properties an index enforces at upload, so every correctly built wheel earns them and they carry no information about how legible the artifact is to an agent. Raised by the miri-py team after five unrelated wheels returned an identical 8/10 in that category. Note `gate` is why weight 0 needs a discriminator: the id pattern reserves the X namespaces for health-only extension checks, which also carry weight 0, and one value cannot mean two things. The corpus contains no X-namespace check today, so the collision is ANTICIPATORY rather than actual - the discriminator is here so that adding the first extension check cannot silently reinterpret the three weight-0 gates that already exist.

weight.description: Conformance-score weight; all active weights per target sum to exactly 100. Weight 0 means the check does not contribute to the score, and `scoring` says why: an extension (X-namespace) check is health-only, a `gate` check is a precondition whose failure makes the artifact non-conforming without being measured.

conditional.description: When the condition does not apply, the check is EXCLUDED FROM BOTH the numerator and the denominator - it is removed from the calculation, exactly as a capability-forfeited check is. It is NOT awarded its weight. This is the not-applicable-is-not-a-pass rule: a check whose condition does not hold has not been satisfied, and scoring it as passed would let an artifact earn weight for an absence. Note the predicate itself is not machine-readable - it is stated in fires_when prose - so a linter decides applicability per check, and MUST report which checks it excluded and why.

severity.description: Canonical severity for health scoring; implementations MUST use these values, not their own

default.description: Severity of each violation of this check (numeric values 1-5 in the same order)

violation_unit.description: What counts as one violation - the countable unit that feeds magnitude-aware health scoring

population_unit.description: Canonical countable population for per-instance checks (the denominator for report-level violation_density). Defined only where a natural population exists; reports MUST carry the population count when this field is present, and MUST omit it otherwise. Never an input to any score.

short_description.description: One-line statement of what the check verifies

references.description: Standards trail: the specs and external standards this check derives from

examples.description: Concrete examples of the check failing and passing

violation.description: A concrete example of a violation

compliant.description: What the conforming state looks like

requirements.description: Operating capabilities beyond the target's baseline analysis mode (static inspection for wheels; local invocation for CLIs) that this check needs. A linter lacking a listed capability MUST skip the check (forfeited, reported) with the fixed reason: network -> network_unavailable, previous-release -> previous_release_unavailable, execution -> execution_disabled; a linter satisfying them MUST NOT skip. Absent or empty means computable from the artifact alone - skipping is non-conforming. PRECEDENCE, where a check is both `conditional` and capability-gated (ten checks are - five python-wheel, five cli): evaluate the CONDITION FIRST. If it provably does not apply the check is EXCLUDED and the capability is irrelevant; if it provably applies and the capability is absent the check is FORFEITED; if whether it applies cannot be settled the check is FORFEITED, because an unsettled condition is ignorance rather than scope. Without this, the sentence above reads as unconditional and a linter implementing it would forfeit MIRI-PY-030 on a first release where the checklists say to exclude it - the same wheel graded `undetermined` by one conforming linter and Gold by another.

rationale.description: Why violating this check is harmful and why the standard checks for it - the editorial case for the check's existence

fires_when.description: Concrete trigger conditions: the situations in which a conforming linter raises this check

remediation.description: Ordered steps to resolve violations; suggested_fix remains the one-line summary

urls.description: Canonical locations of this check: the canonical YAML definition on GitHub and the published HTML page. Embedded so linter reports can link both without deriving them.

definition.description: GitHub URL of this YAML file on main

$schema.description: The interpretation contract this definition is written against. Required, and required to be exact. This is what makes a semantics change loud: a v2 definition carries a key that v1's closed `additionalProperties` rejects, and a v1 definition omits a key v2 requires, so a mismatched pairing fails in both directions instead of validating and scoring wrongly. The same convention the metadata documents already use.

allOf.description: A gate carries no weight and can only be a MUST. Its sole declared effect is non-conformance, and only a MUST can cause that - a SHOULD gate would be inert, which is what the X namespace is for. Previously enforced only by tools/check_consistency.py, which downstream vendors do not run.
